long_biography.plain_text:
A $5,000 loan secured against his parents' home gave John Staluppi his first operating base: a Sunoco station. He made that venture profitable, then persuaded Honda to let him sell its motorcycles when the marque was still little known in America. As Honda moved into cars and fuel prices rose during the 1970s, Staluppi rapidly added franchises.

Within a decade he controlled close to twenty dealerships and later broadened the portfolio through Oldsmobile, Nissan, Hyundai and other marques. Atlantic Automotive Group eventually reached forty locations at its peak, with professional partners taking day-to-day responsibility while Staluppi retained strategic influence. His later work has included classic-car collecting and charity auctions supporting health and community causes.
